title: Dear as Thou Wast, and Justly Dear
description: Dear as Thou Wast, and Justly Dear in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Dale wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 407, “"Weep Not."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Dear as thou wast, and just-ly dear, We would not weep for thee; One thought shall check the start-ing tear, It is that thou art free.

lines: Dear as thou wast, and justly dear,
We would not weep for thee;
One thought shall check the starting tear, —
It is — that thou art free.
And thus shall faith's consoling power
O, who that saw thy parting hour
O, may such grace on us be shed,
And make our end like thine!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Thomas Dale died in 1870.
credits: Words by Thomas Dale (1797–1870), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
